titre: Enrolling my child in preschool or elementary school
resume: Two steps: the town hall (mairie) issues an enrollment certificate, then the school admits the child. The documents to bring, and what changes when the parents are separated.
aQuoiCaSert: Education is compulsory from age 3. To enroll in a public preschool (école maternelle) or elementary school (école élémentaire), you first go to the school affairs department of the town hall (mairie), which gives you an enrollment certificate stating the assigned school. Then the school's principal admits your child on presentation of this certificate and proof of vaccinations. Preparing the documents in advance saves you a second trip.
quiEstConcerne: Parents of a child who turns 3 in the calendar year of the start of the school year.
Parents who are moving or changing their child's school.
Families who have just arrived in Réunion, including with a child who does not yet speak French.
aSavoir: The child must be enrolled in preschool at the start of the school year in the calendar year they turn 3. Enrollment in public school is free.
Enrollment at the town hall must be done by June at the latest before the school year starts. Enrollment usually opens in March, sometimes earlier depending on the town.

ID accepted by the town hall: family record book (livret de famille), ID card, passport or birth certificate extract. A sworn statement (attestation sur l'honneur) may be accepted for both identity and address.
As a rule, children are enrolled in the school of the catchment area set by the town. Another school requires an exemption (dérogation), which is not automatic.

Separated parents: enrolling in or withdrawing from a school is a routine decision. One parent can do it alone and is presumed to have the other's consent, but must inform them. If the other parent tells the school they disagree, the school must take this into account; the family court judge (juge aux affaires familiales, JAF) can decide.
Sole parental authority: if a judgment gives it to only one parent, that parent decides alone. Bring a copy of the judgment.
Vaccines: the list of compulsory vaccines depends on the child's year of birth. There is no vaccination requirement specific to Réunion.
If the school has both a preschool and an elementary section, moving up to CP (first grade) happens automatically.

documents.libelle: The child's family record book, ID card, passport or birth certificate extract
documents.detail: No birth certificate? Request it free of charge online or at the town hall of the place of birth.

documents.libelle: ID of the parent doing the enrollment
documents.detail: ID card, passport or residence permit.
Utility bill, rent receipt or tax notice. If you are living with someone, ask which letter of accommodation the town hall accepts.

documents.libelle: Health record book (carnet de santé, vaccination pages) or certificate of contraindication
documents.detail: A photocopy of the vaccination pages is often requested by the school.

documents.libelle: Judgment or agreement setting parental authority and residence, if you are separated
documents.detail: Copy. Essential in case of sole parental authority.

documents.libelle: Certificat de radiation (withdrawal certificate) from the former school
documents.detail: Only when changing schools. Ask the former school's principal for it.

documents.libelle: Enrollment certificate issued by the town hall
documents.detail: Original to hand to the school's principal. Keep a copy.

etapes.titre: Contact your town hall's school affairs department
etapes.detail: Ask for the enrollment dates, whether you need an appointment, whether there is an online service, and the exact list of documents.
The child's ID or family record book, your ID, recent proof of address, up-to-date health record book, judgment if you are separated, certificat de radiation if changing schools.

etapes.titre: Collect the enrollment certificate at the town hall
etapes.detail: It states the assigned school. Ask for an exemption at this point if you want another school.

etapes.titre: Have your child admitted to the school
etapes.detail: Present the enrollment certificate and proof of vaccinations. Give both parents' contact details and the list of people allowed to pick up the child.
If you are separated, let them know in writing (text message or email).

ou.nom: Your town hall, school affairs department
ou.detail: Enrollment, enrollment certificate and catchment-area exemptions.
Admission of the child and certificat de radiation.
Reception of newly arrived non-French-speaking students: French assessment and placement, requested by the school.

datesLimites.detail: Enrollment often opens in March. Check the dates with your town hall and the school calendar of the académie de La Réunion (regional education authority).

aConfirmer: To be confirmed locally: enrollment dates, appointments, online service and list of documents, specific to each town hall in Réunion.
To be confirmed locally: whether a sworn statement or a letter of accommodation is accepted instead of proof of address, depending on the town hall.
To be confirmed: contact details of the CASNAV de La Réunion, as the académie's pages give different addresses and numbers.
